title: Developer Experience Documentation: SDK Guides, Quickstarts & Top Issues Playbook
author: Maya Patel
summary: Canonical playbook for Developer Experience documentation: standard SDK guide layout, quickstart templates, API example guidance, docs-site publishing procedures, and the top support issues with canonical fixes.
content:
Purpose:

This playbook defines the canonical structure, publishing processes, and maintenance procedures for Developer Experience documentation (SDK guides, quickstarts & templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures) and the top support issues with canonical fixes. The objective is consistent, runnable, and support-reducing documentation that helps developers get value quickly while lowering Support load.

Scope:

- All SDK guides and examples for Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Go, and Java.
- Quickstarts and template repos referenced from the docs site.
- REST and SDK API examples shown in docs.
- Docs-site CI/CD and publishing procedures.
- Top support issues and canonical fixes maintained by DevEx + Support.

Owners and Reviewers:

- Primary owner: Developer Experience (DevEx) team.
- Publishing owner: DevEx docs-owner on-call.
- Reviewers: Product SDK team, Support, Security.

Required structure for every SDK guide:

1) Short title and one-line description.
2) Prerequisites (account, REDWOOD_API_KEY env var, SDK version).
3) Quickstart: copy-paste example that returns a working response in <2 minutes.
4) Concepts & glossary (model, route, streaming vs blocking, batching, function-calls).
5) Common patterns with short examples (chat, streaming, embeddings, reranking).
6) Error handling and retry guidance (401, 429, 422, 503).
7) Configuration examples (timeouts, retry, batching, chunking).
8) Advanced topics (large context handling, pagination, quantization notes, performance tuning).
9) API reference links and SDK changelog.
10) Troubleshooting section linking to canonical fixes and support tickets.

Quickstart template (copyable):

Title: Quickstart 1 Python SDK (3 minutes)
Prereqs: Python 3.10+, pip, REDWOOD_API_KEY in env.
Purpose: Minimal chat completion + streaming example.

Copy-paste example (Python):

# quickstart_python.py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import os

client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
response = client.chat.create(model='redwood-large-1', messages=[{'role':'user','content':'Translate to French: "Good morning"'}])
print('full response:', response.text)

# streaming example (pseudo)
for chunk in client.chat.stream(model='redwood-large-1', messages=[{'role':'user','content':'Write a haiku about coffee.'}]):
    print(chunk.text, end='')

Notes: Quickstarts must be runnable locally without additional infra (no DBs, no SSO). If an API key is required, specify exact env var names and how to obtain them.

API examples guidance:

- Provide at least two examples per API surface: minimal blocking call (curl + SDK) and streaming/advanced usage.
- Include error-handling examples for 401, 429 (rate limit), 422 (invalid payload), and 503 (transient capacity).
- Keep in-doc examples <= 60 lines; link to template repos for longer integrations.

Example: REST curl minimal generation:

curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-medium-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the bullet points in 3 sentences."}]}'

Example: JavaScript (Node) snippet:

import Redwood from 'redwood-js'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
const resp = await client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-medium-1', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Explain continuous batching.' }] })
console.log(resp.output[0].text)

Docs-site operating procedures (publishing & QA):

1) Create a staging branch named docs/<short-name>-YYYYMMDD in the docs repo.
2) Run automated linting (markdownlint) and link-check.
3) Add smoke-test scripts under docs/ci/smoke to verify quickstarts run with a test API key (Docker runner).
4) Submit PR; include reviewers: devex, sdk-owner, support.
5) PR checklist: TL;DR, smoke-test pass link, and runnable quickstart.
6) Merge only after approvals; staging deploy runs automatically. Keep staging up for 24 hours for soak testing.
7) Deployment cadence: daily canary deploys for non-breaking docs; coordinated release for breaking changes.

Versioning and breaking changes:

- Docs versioning aligns with major SDK versions.
- Breaking SDK changes require migration guide, deprecation timeline (>=30 days), and example diffs.
- Use a visible legacy banner for removed behaviors for 90 days post-release.

Mandatory CI checks for doc PRs:

- markdownlint: no style violations.
- link-check: internal links resolve in staging.
- example-snippets: execute smoke tests for executable code blocks.
- docspell-check: ensure no secrets, tokens, or customer PII are included.

Top support issues and canonical fixes (maintainable list):

1) Auth: 401 Unauthorized
   - Symptom: API returns 401.
   - Causes: missing/rotated API key, wrong env var, key scoped to another org.
   - Canonical fix: Verify REDWOOD_API_KEY env var, run curl -I -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health. If 200, confirm SDK uses same env var; otherwise rotate and update secrets manager.

2) Rate limit: 429 Too Many Requests
   - Symptom: Bursty 429s with Retry-After.
   - Cause: unbounded parallel requests or lack of batching.
   - Canonical fix: Implement exponential backoff with jitter (base 500ms) and enable SDK client-side batching or use Redwood batching route configuration.

# simple exponential backoff pseudocode (python)
import time, random
retries = 0
while retries < 5:
    resp = client.chat.create(...)
    if resp.status_code == 429:
        time.sleep((2 ** retries) * 0.5 + random.random() * 0.1)
        retries += 1
        continue
    break

3) Streaming disconnects / partial outputs
   - Symptom: Stream ends prematurely with truncated output.
   - Cause: network timeouts, proxies closing idle connections, or client chunk handling bugs.
   - Canonical fix: Increase client read timeout, enable keep-alive, validate proxies allow long-lived connections, and provide non-stream fallback.

4) Model mismatch / 422 Invalid payload
   - Symptom: 422 or immediate model rejection.
   - Cause: Incorrect payload shape or unsupported feature used with smaller model.
   - Canonical fix: Validate payload against SDK examples; use model-profile table to determine supported features.

5) Tokenization / context length issues
   - Symptom: Outputs cut off; implicit truncation.
   - Cause: Assuming tokens == characters; large system messages or embeddings exceed model window.
   - Canonical fix: Provide token-count utilities (link to tokenizer library) and recommend chunking/prefix caching strategies.

Maintaining the Top Issues list:

- Owner: DevEx + Support triage rotation (monthly).
- Process: Support spikes require creating/updating a canonical fix doc within 2 business days.
- Tag docs with label support-canonical and link to ticket IDs in related_pages.

Canonical templates and repos:

- Quickstart templates: github.com/redwood-inference/devex-quickstarts (branches: python, node, go).
- SDK examples: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples (per-language folders).
- Docs CI runner: github.com/redwood-inference/docs-ci (Docker-based smoke runners).

Checklist before creating a new SDK guide or quickstart:

- Confirm owner & reviewer list in the PR.
- Include a runnable quickstart that completes in <2 minutes.
- Add error handling examples for 401/429/422/503.
- Ensure no secrets/keys embedded in examples.
- Run doc linting and snippet smoke-tests.
- Add labels: sdk, language, support-canonical (if applicable).

Maintenance and deprecation policy:

- Review SDK guides quarterly for alignment with the latest SDK release.
- Deprecate examples relying on removed endpoints; provide migration notes and example diffs.

Appendix: example model capability table (to include in SDK guide pages)

Model family | Streaming | Function-calls | Max context | Recommended use
redwood-small | no | limited | 8k | low-latency embeddings, small prompts
redwood-medium | yes | partial | 32k | general-purpose chat and completion
redwood-large | yes | full | 128k | long-context assistants, summarization

(Authoritative values should be pulled from the live model-catalog endpoint; update this table during model onboarding.)

Contact and escalation:

- Docs publishing issues: @devex-docs on Slack.
- Product-impacting changes: open an RFC in product-docs and notify Support.
- Emergency rollback: docs-owner approves immediate revert and notifies #prod-ops.

This playbook is the canonical reference for Developer Experience documentation. Keep content concise, runnable, and link to template repos for long integrations. Update this page during quarterly doc reviews or when new recurring support patterns emerge.
